references.text: Joshua conquered the whole land: the hill country, the Negev and the lowland—the same geographical areas mentioned in Judges 1:9, showing Judah's continued conquest of these regions.
Describes Joshua's conquest of the hill country, the Negev and the lowland, the same three geographical regions that the tribe of Judah continued to conquer.
Describes the cities in the lowland (Shephelah) that were allotted to the tribe of Judah, which they later fought to conquer.
Moses describes the land as the mountains, the lowland and the Negev—the same geographical areas that Judah was to occupy.
Mentions the Canaanites living in the lowland, the same people that the tribe of Judah fought against in Judges 1:9.
Mentions the kings in the hill country, the lowland and the coast—the same geographical areas described in Judges 1:9.
